newsitem.title: USA: Decision on LILCO temporary rates delayed.
newsitem.headline: Decision on LILCO temporary rates delayed.

text.p: The New York State Public Service Commission has postponed its decision on Long Island Lighting Co's temporary rates, commission spokesman Dave Flanagan said.
In July the commission ordered an expedited proceeding to consider temporary electric rates for LILCO and said it expected to issue a decision by September 11.
Flanagan said the case is no longer on the agenda for the commission's September 11 meeting. The next possible time for the commission to take it up would be October 2, he added.

An advocacy staff team of the state's Department of Public Service filed a temporary rate proposal with the commission recommending a 5.2 percent LILCO rate cut effective October 1, the department said. The proposal was made in response to the commission's call for consideration of temporary rates.
The staff did not propose changing the LILCO Ratemaking and Performance Plan that was part of the Shoreham nuclear power plant settlement, the department's summary of the proposal noted.
It did call for about $66.1 million a year in base rate reductions and $24.1 million in fuel cost reductions.
The staff also called for the reductions to "be applied differently to different service classifications to partially correct existing imbalances among the rate classes."

The summary noted the staff used the sales, revenue and cost of equity forecasts LILCO filed with the commission on March 8, projecting an equity cost of 11.0 percent this year, 10.7 percent next year, 10.52 percent in 1998, 10.38 percent in 1999 and 10.25 percent in 2000.

The staff supported its proposal by noting funds LILCO has comming or on hand, and calling for a $5 million annual property tax reduction, a $2.9 million annual reduction in the utility's base capitalization and a $55.7 million annual reduction in its operation and maintenance expenses.
Stating this would represent a 15 percent cut in yearly maintenance spending, LILCO said this would "have serious consequences for customer service and system reliability."
To achieve such cuts, the company said Thursday, it would "have to slash programs like storm restoration, tree trimming, and electric line maintenance."
The funds coming and on hand noted by the staff include $5 million for LILCO's 18 percent share of the expected $27 million under run in Nine Mile 2 nuclear power plant costs.

The other owners of the plant, located east of Rochester, N.Y., on Lake Ontario, are the operator, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, with 41 percent, New York State Electric and Gas Corp 18 percent and Central Hudson Gas and Electric Corp 9 percent.

The staff also cited $11.2 million the New York Power Authority agreed to pay LILCO in a settlement, the utility's overcollection of $26 million under the Shoreham ratemaking plan, and Suffolk County property tax refunds totaling $176 million. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
